attribution_limits: Route-ownership roots are diagnostic failure-before plus safety-control evidence; they do not implement a receipt protocol or establish a production fix.
The known-service oracle deliberately supplies fixture knowledge. Its failure is design evidence that does not validate a production estimator or throughput acceptance.
Logical delivery, exact observed RTT, and multi-route physical drain remain distinct review concepts.
Raw logs, source, overlays, binaries, local paths, and identifiers are excluded; normalized numerical rows, outcomes, and hash pins are retained.
oracle_counterfactual: On exact hybrid+common-bound, force measure() to return12500000B/s at or after the known4s propagation step. Readonly calls do not retain. Before4s behavior unchanged. Actual RTT, raw recovery, pacing contracts, windows, queues, losses and ACK policy unchanged.
oracle_limitations: Known physical capacity is an oracle supplied by the fixture; no claim that existing feedback identifies it.
This is one same-input diagnostic comparison, not a repeat-until-pass campaign.
Cumulative recovery counters include warmup and cannot alone explain measurement-interval loss.
The original frozen average/minflow/measured-drop gates apply; stronger per-interval shared gate was not present in this copied fixture.
Receipt protocol remains review-only and no new timer exception is proposed.
oracle_scope: known-service oracle diagnostic only; not a production estimator and no performance acceptance
receipt_review_scope: review-only measured observed RTT receipt; logical delivery is distinct from physical-prefix/drain proof
route_limits: Actual client send workers, actual H1 route writes and production ACK coalescer; receiver ACKs are injected with current original/duplicate wire shapes.
Virtual time and barriers; no wall-clock sleep used as proof.
The early ACK during the retry write is allowed to be ignored because the resend queue temporarily omits that item.
Multi-route control explicitly leaves the original physical copy unconsumed in route A; a newer route B cumulative head is insufficient to certify route A.
No receipt protocol implemented; new identity alone cannot prove all physical routes drained.
All buffers and client worker lifecycles reconciled by assertMessagePoolOwnership.
route_ownership_scope: diagnostic failure-before and safety control only; no production fix, nonce implementation or performance attribution
